title: A value scanner
hints: Store the results as a `std::map<std::uint64_t, double>`: the address and the value seen at the last scan. A map keeps the addresses sorted, and every comparison scan has the previous value right there.

Converting every type to `double` for comparisons keeps one code path: an `int32_t` fits exactly in a `double`, and so does a `float`. Only the equality test needs to know the type (exact for integers, a tolerance for floating point).
requirements: Typed reads with correct size, alignment and region bounds.
Exact scans with float tolerance, and unknown-value first scans.
All the comparison scans, using values remembered from the previous scan.
Unreadable results are dropped; results are always sorted.
stretch: Add a "snapshot of the whole process" function for real use: on your own running program, walk its memory with `VirtualQueryEx`, keep committed private regions that are readable and writable, and copy them with `ReadProcessMemory` into a `Snapshot`. Then try the scanner on a small game you wrote.
